source: 2019 Alabama Course of Study: Mathematics, Grade 2 (2.1-2.27), standard text verified Nov 24, 2026 against the official ALSDE 2019 Course of Study PDF. Domains/clusters are the standard Alabama groupings. No DIGS critical flags exist for 2nd grade in Eddie's files, so critical is false for all — do not treat that as a DIGS marking.

standards.cluster: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.
standards.text: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve one- and two-step word problems by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem. Second grade problem types include adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing with unknowns in all positions.

standards.cluster: Add and subtract within 20.

parts.text: State automatically all sums of two one-digit numbers.

standards.text: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies such as counting on, making ten, decomposing a number leading to ten, using the relationship between addition and subtraction, and creating equivalent but easier or known sums.

standards.cluster: Work with equal groups of objects to gain foundations for multiplication.

parts.text: Write an equation to express an even number as a sum of two equal addends.

standards.text: Use concrete objects to determine whether a group of up to 20 objects is even or odd.

standards.cluster: Work with equal groups of objects to gain foundations for multiplication.

parts.text: Write an equation to express the total number of objects in a rectangular array with up to 5 rows and up to 5 columns as a sum of equal addends.

standards.text: Using concrete and pictorial representations and repeated addition, determine the total number of objects in a rectangular array with up to 5 rows and up to 5 columns.

standards.cluster: Understand simple patterns.
standards.text: Reproduce, extend, create, and describe patterns and sequences using a variety of materials.

standards.cluster: Understand place value.

parts.text: Explain the following three-digit numbers as special cases: 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens, called a 'hundred,' and the numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0 ones).

standards.text: Explain that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones.

standards.cluster: Understand place value.
standards.text: Count within 1000 by ones, fives, tens, and hundreds.

standards.cluster: Understand place value.
standards.text: Read and write numbers to 1000 using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.

standards.cluster: Understand place value.
standards.text: Compare two three-digit numbers based on the value of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits, recording the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, and < and orally with the words 'is greater than,' 'is equal to,' and 'is less than.'

standards.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
standards.text: Fluently add and subtract within 100, using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

standards.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
standards.text: Use a variety of strategies to add up to four two-digit numbers.

standards.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.

parts.text: Explain that in adding or subtracting three-digit numbers, one adds or subtracts hundreds and hundreds, tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose or decompose tens or hundreds.

standards.text: Add and subtract within 1000 using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method.

standards.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
standards.text: Mentally add and subtract 10 or 100 to a given number between 100 and 900.

standards.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
standards.text: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations. Explanations may be supported by drawings or objects.

standards.cluster: Collect and analyze data and interpret results.

parts.text: Create a line plot where the horizontal scale is marked off in whole-number units to show the lengths of several measured objects.

standards.text: Measure lengths of several objects to the nearest whole unit.

standards.cluster: Collect and analyze data and interpret results.

parts.text: Using information presented in a bar graph, solve simple 'put-together,' 'take-apart,' and 'compare' problems.
Using Venn diagrams, pictographs, and 'yes-no' charts, analyze data to predict an outcome.

standards.text: Create a picture graph and bar graph to represent data with up to four categories.

standards.cluster: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.
standards.text: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using standard units of measurement shown on rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, or measuring tapes.

standards.cluster: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.
standards.text: Measure objects with two different units, and describe how the two measurements relate to each other and the size of the unit chosen.

standards.cluster: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.
standards.text: Estimate lengths using the following standard units of measurement: inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.

standards.cluster: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.
standards.text: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference of the two objects using standard units of length.

standards.cluster: Relate addition and subtraction to length.
standards.text: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve word problems involving same units of length, representing the problem with drawings (such as drawings of rulers) and/or equations with a symbol for the unknown number.

standards.cluster: Relate addition and subtraction to length.
standards.text: Create a number line diagram using whole numbers and use it to represent whole-number sums and differences within 100.

standards.cluster: Work with time and money.

parts.text: Express an understanding of common terms such as, but not limited to, quarter past, half past, and quarter to.

standards.text: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.

standards.cluster: Work with time and money.

parts.text: Identify nickels and quarters by name and value.
Find the value of a collection of quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies.
Solve word problems by adding and subtracting within one dollar, using the $ and cent symbols appropriately (not including decimal notation). Example: 24 cents + 26 cents = 50 cents.

standards.text: Solve problems with money.

standards.cluster: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

parts.text: Recognize and draw shapes having specified attributes. Examples: a given number of angles or a given number of equal faces.

standards.text: Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes.

standards.cluster: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
standards.text: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares, and count to find the total number of squares.

standards.cluster: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

parts.text: Explain that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.

standards.text: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares. Describe the shares using such terms as halves, thirds, half of, or a third of, and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds, or four fourths.
